newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: ANZ Bank stays in the black but faces jobs showdown.
newsitem.headline: ANZ Bank stays in the black but faces jobs showdown.

text.p: Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Ltd said on Wednesday that growth in loans and fee income had offset a first quarter squeeze on interest margins, but the bank did not ease workers' concerns about job cuts.

"The anticipated fall in interest margins in Australia is occurring ... however this is being offset by continued growth in lending assets and increased fee income," ANZ chairman Charles Goode told the group's annual meeting.
Goode did not disclose figures, but said tight margins had flowed particularly from reductions in mortgage lending rates.

Stiff competition from new entrants in the Australian mortgage market and cuts by the Reserve Bank of Australia in official interest rates during 1996 had forced banks to reduce interest rates for most banking products.

But despite keeping its head above water, the ANZ faces an industrial showdown over branch closures and job cuts expected to result from a shift in the banking industry away from traditional branch networks towards electronic delivery.

Finance Sector Union (FSU) joint national secretary Tony Beck told the meeting that ANZ was the only bank in Australia not to have reached an agreement with unions on the way the restructuring for the bank industry would be carried out.
"This is the only bank where we are encountering so many difficulties in reaching a sensitive understanding on the way this reform will proceed," he said.
Industrial unrest over potential job losses at the bank peaked in November last year when ANZ union members went on strike for a day, claiming the bank planned to shed as many as 5,000 jobs.

At a news conference after the annual meeting, Goode said the bank had not set staff reduction targets but it and the union agreed that cuts necessitated by industry change should occur through natural attrition.
At September 30, 1996, ANZ had 23,727 employees and 1,070 branches Australia-wide.
Meanwhile, the ANZ said it was not looking to take over another bank or be a takeover target itself.
Offshore, the bank was focused squarely on further expansion which was expected to help underpin group profit growth, the chairman said.

"There is significant potential growth to come from the globalisation of our investment banking and cards businesses and we will also be actively looking for opportunities to expand our funds management operations," he said.

ANZ reported a net profit of A$1.12 billion ($874 million) for the year to September 30, up from A$1.05 billion in the previous year, but said when it released its results in November that it expected margins to contract further in the year ahead.
